That covers the demotion case, but not the general case the removed sentence covered. The defect I actually found at v4 was a retroactive relabel of reMeasurementAtV3, not a demotion; this generation's edits to the V3 and V6 notes are likewise relabels, and they are rostered by good practice rather than by any surviving rule.
advisories.whyNotAShouldFix: Nothing in v8 is falsified. The roster claim is true — my diff finds 23 changed paths and zero uncovered — and the removal weakens a prophylactic, not a current statement of fact. No finding I make here depends on it, and the exemption was not invoked. I considered SHOULD-FIX on the ground that quiet erosion of a self-imposed guardrail is exactly what this chain exists to catch, and decline it because severity should track what is presently wrong rather than what could later go wrong; the v9 roster audit would catch any exploitation, as the v4 and v5 audits did.
